source_evidence.observation: The proposition takes a random variable X and asserts the equivalence of four existence properties, with positive parameters K1 through K4: a two-sided sub-gaussian tail bound, square-root growth of all Lp norms for p >= 1, a local exponential-moment bound for lambda^2 X^2, and a one-point exponential-square bound.

source_evidence.anchor: Footnote 4 attached to the sentence about the parameters differing by an absolute constant factor
source_evidence.observation: The quantitative meaning is that there is one absolute constant C such that, for any applicable ordered pair of properties i and j, property i with parameter Ki yields property j with a parameter Kj satisfying Kj <= C Ki.

source_evidence.anchor: Proposition 2.5.2, paragraph beginning 'Moreover, if E X = 0' and item (v)
source_evidence.observation: Only under the additional centering condition E X = 0 does the proposition add a fifth equivalent property: existence of K5 > 0 such that E exp(lambda X) <= exp(K5^2 lambda^2) for every real lambda.

source_evidence.anchor: Displayed formulas in items (i)-(v), followed by proof headings i=>ii, ii=>iii, iii=>iv, iv=>i and the sentence introducing iii=>v and v=>i
source_evidence.observation: The formulas and proof structure preserve two distinct equivalence cycles: (i)-(iv) without centering, and the extension to (v) after assuming centering; the squared-exponential property (iii) is required only on |lambda| <= 1/K3, whereas property (v) is required for all lambda in R.

binders: X is a (implicitly real-valued) random variable. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, Proposition 2.5.2 opening: 'Let X be a random variable'; real-valuedness is structurally indicated by |X|, X^2, and lambda in R in items (i)-(v).)
For property (i), K1 is existentially quantified with K1 > 0, and t ranges over all real t >= 0. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, item (i).)
For property (ii), K2 is existentially quantified with K2 > 0, and p ranges over all p >= 1. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, item (ii).)
For property (iii), K3 is existentially quantified with K3 > 0, and lambda ranges over real values satisfying |lambda| <= 1/K3. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, item (iii).)
For property (iv), K4 is existentially quantified with K4 > 0. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, item (iv).)
For property (v), when E X = 0, K5 is existentially quantified with K5 > 0, and lambda ranges over every real number. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, centered extension and item (v).)
There exists an absolute constant C controlling conversion of witnesses between any two properties in the applicable equivalence family. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, footnote 4.)
hypotheses: The base assertion assumes only that X is a random variable; no centering hypothesis is imposed for the equivalence of (i)-(iv). (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, opening of Proposition 2.5.2 through item (iv).)
The equivalence with property (v) has the additional hypothesis E X = 0. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, paragraph immediately before item (v).)
conclusions: Properties (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv), each understood as existence of its own positive witness Ki, are equivalent. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, Proposition 2.5.2 opening and items (i)-(iv).)

Quantitatively, there is an absolute C such that an applicable property (i) with witness Ki implies an applicable property (j) with some witness Kj <= C Ki; thus the equivalence controls the scale parameters up to a universal factor. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, footnote 4.)
If E X = 0, properties (i)-(iv) are also equivalent to property (v). (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, centered extension and item (v).)
definitions_and_conventions: Property (i): P{|X| >= t} <= 2 exp(-t^2/K1^2) for every t >= 0. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, item (i).)
Property (ii): ||X||_{L^p} is explicitly identified with (E |X|^p)^(1/p), and it obeys ||X||_{L^p} <= K2 sqrt(p) for every p >= 1. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, item (ii).)
Property (iii): E exp(lambda^2 X^2) <= exp(K3^2 lambda^2) for every lambda with |lambda| <= 1/K3. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, item (iii).)
Property (iv): E exp(X^2/K4^2) <= 2. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, item (iv).)
Property (v): E exp(lambda X) <= exp(K5^2 lambda^2) for every lambda in R. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, item (v).)

Each Ki is strictly positive; the same numerical witness is not required for different properties. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, opening sentence and the repeated phrases 'There exists Ki > 0' in items (i)-(v).)

'Absolute constant' means the comparison factor C is uniform rather than depending on X, i, j, or the particular witness. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, opening sentence and footnote 4; uniformity is the standard structural content of 'there exists an absolute constant C' before the universal choice of i and j.)
implicit_context: Probability P and expectation E refer to the law of the same random variable X on its underlying probability space. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, common use of P and E throughout items (i)-(v).)

The source treats X as scalar and real-valued, though the codomain is not restated explicitly in the proposition. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, structural use of absolute value, squares, order comparisons, and real lambda.)
The centering clause scopes only the addition of property (v), not the equivalence of properties (i)-(iv). (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, placement of 'Moreover, if E X = 0' after item (iv).)

The footnote's reference to properties 1 through 5 must be read within the main statement's applicability condition for (v), namely E X = 0. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, footnote 4 together with the immediately preceding centered extension.)

details: Without any centering assumption, all four existential assertions (i)-(iv) are mutually equivalent. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, proposition opening and items (i)-(iv).)
Under E X = 0, the fifth existential assertion is mutually equivalent with all four earlier assertions. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, centered extension and item (v).)

The result is stronger than bare logical equivalence: every applicable implication i=>j permits a target witness Kj no larger than C times the starting witness Ki for one absolute C. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, footnote 4.)
The properties use separate witnesses K1,...,K5; they are comparable, not asserted equal. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, opening sentence and items (i)-(v).)
The tail is two-sided through |X|, includes the boundary event >= t, carries prefactor 2, and is required at every nonnegative t. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, item (i).)
The bound concerns absolute Lp moments and grows as sqrt(p), uniformly over every p >= 1. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, item (ii).)
Property (iii) uses exp(lambda^2 X^2), compares its expectation with exp(K3^2 lambda^2), and restricts lambda to the closed neighborhood |lambda| <= 1/K3. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, item (iii).)
Property (iv) evaluates at the scale K4 through exp(X^2/K4^2) and uses the numerical upper bound 2. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, item (iv).)
Property (v) is conditional on E X = 0, concerns exp(lambda X) rather than exp(lambda^2 X^2), and is global in lambda in R. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, centered extension and item (v).)
The parameter inequalities Ki > 0 are strict. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, each item (i)-(v).)
The domains include t = 0, p = 1, and the endpoints lambda = +/-1/K3 in property (iii). (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, the displayed quantifier ranges in items (i)-(iii).)
No analogous centering assumption is part of properties (i)-(iv). (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, placement of the centered extension after item (iv).)

undebatable_constraints: The contract must preserve all four base properties (i)-(iv) and their mutual equivalence, rather than selecting only one characterization. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, Proposition 2.5.2 opening and items (i)-(iv).)
Property (i) must be a two-sided absolute-value tail bound P{|X| >= t} <= 2 exp(-t^2/K1^2) for all t >= 0. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, item (i).)
Property (ii) must quantify all p >= 1 and use the absolute-moment Lp norm (E|X|^p)^(1/p) <= K2 sqrt(p). (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, item (ii).)
Property (iii) must retain both the exact squared-exponential form E exp(lambda^2 X^2) <= exp(K3^2 lambda^2) and its local domain |lambda| <= 1/K3. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, item (iii).)
Property (iv) must retain the one-point threshold E exp(X^2/K4^2) <= 2. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, item (iv).)
Property (v) must be included only in the centered extension E X = 0, and there it must hold for every real lambda. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, centered extension and item (v).)
All Ki witnesses must be strictly positive and property-specific. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, repeated existential clauses in items (i)-(v).)

The quantitative absolute-factor comparison must be preserved: for every applicable implication i=>j, a witness Kj can be chosen with Kj <= C Ki for a universal C. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, footnote 4.)

ambiguities.issue: The proposition says only 'random variable' and does not explicitly name its codomain.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, Proposition 2.5.2 opening; items (i)-(v) then use |X|, X^2, order comparisons, and lambda in R.
ambiguities.impact: A formal rendering must choose a scalar domain. The displayed operations strongly indicate a real-valued random variable, but that typing is inherited mathematical convention rather than an explicit binder in the sentence.

ambiguities.issue: The source writes 'for all p >= 1' without explicitly declaring whether p ranges over real numbers or integers.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, item (ii), which uses L^p notation and (E|X|^p)^(1/p).
ambiguities.impact: Standard Lp usage indicates real p >= 1; restricting to integer p would be a literal domain restriction unless separately shown equivalent with comparable constants.

ambiguities.issue: Footnote 4 says 'for any two properties i, j = 1,...,5' even though property (v) is introduced only under E X = 0.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, centered paragraph before item (v) and footnote 4 below it.
ambiguities.impact: The main statement controls scope: conversions involving (v) apply in the centered case. Reading the footnote as removing the centering condition would contradict the proposition's explicit conditional clause.

contract_plain_english: For any scalar real random variable X, four ways of saying that X has sub-gaussian size are equivalent: its two-sided tails decay like exp(-t^2/K1^2); every absolute Lp norm is at most K2 sqrt(p); the exponential moment of lambda^2 X^2 has the stated quadratic bound for |lambda| <= 1/K3; and one exponential-square moment at scale K4 is at most 2. Each assertion has its own positive scale parameter, and an absolute universal constant converts a witness for any one applicable property into a witness for any other with at most constant-factor enlargement. If X is centered, E X = 0, these are also equivalent to the global MGF bound E exp(lambda X) <= exp(K5^2 lambda^2) for every real lambda. (PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, Proposition 2.5.2 items (i)-(v) and footnote 4; PDF p. 14, printed p. 25, proof structure confirming the two equivalence cycles.)
